title: Bitwise AND of a Number Range
statement: A sensor logs consecutive frame IDs and you need the bits that stay on across an entire capture window. Given two non-negative integers left and right with left <= right (values can be as large as about 2^40, so the window may contain billions of IDs), return the bitwise AND of every integer in the inclusive range [left, right]. When left == right the answer is that single number. Iterating over the range one number at a time is far too slow for the largest windows; aim for a solution whose running time depends on the number of bits, not the size of the range. Return the result as an int.
reference_solution:
def range_bitwise_and(left, right):
    shifts = 0
    while left != right:
        left >>= 1
        right >>= 1
        shifts += 1
    return left << shifts
hints: ANDing many consecutive numbers zeroes out any bit that flips even once in the range. Which bits can possibly survive the whole window?

Only the common binary prefix of left and right survives: below the highest differing bit, every pattern occurs, so every lower bit gets zeroed. Right-shift both endpoints until they are equal, counting the shifts.

Loop while left != right: shift both right by 1 and increment a counter. When they meet, the value is the shared prefix; shift it back left by the counter (left << shifts) and return that. Do not forget the shift back, and note zero shifts happen when left == right.
